subject: AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace & procurement path - next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Aman Gupta <aman@lumenai.com>, Jared Holt <jared.holt@lumenai.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lumenai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T15:23:00Z
Subject: AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace & procurement path - next steps

Hi Aman / Jared / Procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation about the inference workload and cost/latency targets. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Procurement readiness: you mentioned finance prefers PO for anything >$50k ARR but the initial POC could be card. Can you confirm PO vs card preference for the pilot?
- Marketplace interest: you said LumenAI is evaluating AWS Marketplace first. Do you want us to pursue AWS Marketplace registration now, or go direct and convert later?
- Paperwork: we typically provide a W-9, SOC 2 summary, and a short SOW for pilot scope + pricing. I'll attach a draft pricing sheet and a stub SOW for your review.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx, redwood-draft-sow.pdf

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm procurement path (PO vs card) and whether AWS Marketplace is required for purchase.
2) If PO: share target PO date and procurement contact who will own vendor onboarding.
3) If Marketplace: confirm whether you prefer Marketplace SaaS listing (consolidated billing) or an AWS Private Offer (direct contract + marketplace billing).

If easier, happy to schedule a 20-minute call with finance + procurement to align.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
From: Aman Gupta <aman@lumenai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Holt <jared.holt@lumenai.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lumenai.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T17:02:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace & procurement path - next steps

Thanks Camila — quick answers from our side: 

- Marketplace: AWS is preferred, and we'd like to keep the initial production purchase through AWS Marketplace if possible because that simplifies our billing and internal approvals.
- Procurement method: for the POC <$10k we can use a company card, but production will be PO-based. So we need both paths supported.
- Vendor onboarding: procurement will need SOC 2 Type II evidence (or a shared summary), a completed W-9, and a short vendor questionnaire. Jared here is leading finance and will own the PO when we get to that stage.

Can you send the W-9 and SOC 2 summary? Also, is Redwood open to an AWS Private Offer (we'd sign a marketplace private offer rather than a direct Redwood contract) — that keeps everything in AWS for us.

— Aman
Aman Gupta | Head of Platform, LumenAI
aman@lumenai.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Aman Gupta <aman@lumenai.com>, Jared Holt <jared.holt@lumenai.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lumenai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace & procurement path - next steps

On Wed, Jul 1, 2026 at 17:02, Aman Gupta <aman@lumenai.com> wrote:
> Thanks Camila — quick answers from our side:
> - Marketplace: AWS is preferred...

Thanks for the clarity, Aman — really helpful. I've attached the W-9 and a short SOC 2 summary, plus the pricing sheet and a draft SOW for the POC so finance can see quantities and units.

Attachments in this message: redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx, redwood-draft-sow.pdf, redwood-w9.pdf

Below is a brief summary of procurement/commercial paths and trade-offs to help you pick: 

1) AWS Marketplace (SaaS listing or Private Offer)
   - Pros: consolidated billing, easier approvals for teams that prefer marketplace procurement, AWS takes care of licensing transactions.
   - Cons: vendor registration + onboarding with AWS required (can take 2–4 weeks); Private Offer adds a step but lets us include negotiated terms while keeping marketplace billing.

2) Direct Redwood contract + PO (standard enterprise flow)
   - Pros: faster vendor-start for direct billing if finance accepts PO; flexible contract language/SLAs.
   - Cons: some teams prefer marketplace for single-pane billing and procurement tracking.

3) Card for initial pilot
   - Pros: fastest to get started.
   - Cons: not suitable for long-term production purchases >$50k ARR per your note.

Action items proposed: 
- Aman/Jared: confirm whether you'd like us to initiate AWS vendor onboarding (we can kick off the marketplace registration) or proceed with direct contract + PO.
- If PO or Private Offer: please share the procurement owner's email (Jared noted he'll own the PO) and target PO date.
- We'll prepare an AWS Private Offer template if you want marketplace + negotiated terms.

If helpful, I'll set up a short call between Jared, our finance ops (Dylan), and Marissa (CS) to map the onboarding steps.

Thanks — Camila
From: Procurement Team <procurement@lumenai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Aman Gupta <aman@lumenai.com>
Cc: Jared Holt <jared.holt@lumenai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-06T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace & procurement path - next steps

Hi Camila / Aman,

Quick procurement response:

- LumenAI preference: AWS Marketplace (SaaS or Private Offer) for production purchases. For the pilot, card is acceptable.
- Required docs: Completed W-9 (received), SOC 2 Type II report or a vendor SOC summary (we've received the summary but will need a formal report during onboarding).
- Vendor onboarding: Please provide the following to accelerate registration:
   1) Company W-9 (attached, received)
   2) SOC 2 summary and point-of-contact for security answers
   3) Standard payment terms (Net 30) and an example invoice template

We will start the vendor intake this week once we have the SOC contact and a brief vendor questionnaire answered. For Private Offer: Jared will coordinate with Aman and legal to accept invoice terms; target PO issuance date is 2026-08-03 (end of quarter) if everything is in place.

Thanks — Procurement Team
procurement@lumenai.com
